name: Joseph Barsabbas
title: Candidate for the Apostleship
summary: Joseph Barsabbas, also called Justus, was one of two candidates proposed to replace Judas Iscariot as the twelfth apostle. He had followed Jesus throughout his entire public ministry, from John's baptism to the ascension. Although the lot fell on Matthias instead of him, Joseph remained a faithful disciple in the early church.

keyEvents.title: Nominated as an Apostolic Candidate
keyEvents.description: After Jesus' ascension, the congregation proposed Joseph Barsabbas, called Justus, along with Matthias, as candidates to replace Judas Iscariot among the twelve apostles.

keyEvents.title: The Casting of Lots
keyEvents.description: The congregation prayed and cast lots between Joseph Barsabbas and Matthias. The lot fell on Matthias, who was counted as the twelfth apostle.

keyEvents.title: Qualified as an Eyewitness to Jesus' Ministry
keyEvents.description: Joseph Barsabbas was recognized as one who had been with Jesus from John's baptism until the ascension, and was thus an eyewitness to Jesus' resurrection.

keyEvents.title: Part of the praying congregation in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Before the election of a new apostle, Joseph Barsabbas was among the approximately 120 believers gathered in prayer in the upper room in Jerusalem.
